subject: Post-demo: latency targets & streaming behavior — next steps
messages:
From: Sarah Lopez <s.lopez@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: latency targets & streaming behavior — next steps

Marcus / team,

Thanks again for the demo today — the streaming demo and the concurrency behavior were helpful. A quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can map this into our SLOs and the procurement review: 

1) Current baseline (what we measure today on CloudLP): p95 E2E (client -> CloudLP -> response) = ~210ms for short prompts (<= 40 tokens); p99 = ~610ms. Under load (50 concurrent users sending short chat requests) we see p95 ~320ms.

2) Our target SLOs we'd like you to validate for Hosted Redwood: p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 450ms for the main interactive chat endpoint (streaming enabled). For batch/rerank jobs we care more about throughput than strict p99.

3) Traffic mix: 70% short interactive (<= 40 tokens), 20% medium (40–256 tokens), 10% long (>256 tokens). Average arrival rate ~120 reqs/s, with peak bursts up to 350 reqs/s for <60s.

4) Streaming behavior questions: how does Redwood measure E2E when streaming (first-byte vs final-token p95/p99)? Does your hosted product provide per-token latency breakdowns or just end-to-end?

5) Concurrency: our browser clients open a single streaming connection per user. How many concurrent streams per tenant do you support and how does batching affect per-stream latency?

We've attached a small sample of production logs (anonymized) so you can map request sizes to our percentiles.

Next steps we'd like from Redwood: a short doc with expected p95/p99 numbers for our traffic mix, recommended config (model variant, concurrency limits, batching settings), and a one-day spike test run we can schedule to compare apples-to-apples.

Can we aim to schedule the spike test the week of Dec 6? Also — minor admin Q: we need confirmation on data residency for logs (US-only).

Thanks,
Sarah Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme_latency_sample_logs.csv (CSV, 120KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lopez <s.lopez@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency targets & streaming behavior — next steps

Sarah — great notes and thanks for the logs. High-level: we are confident we can achieve the interactive SLOs you listed with our Hosted API in the US region, but we want to validate against your arrival pattern and burst profile.

Immediate next steps from our side: 
- Aditya will map your sample logs to a targeted test plan (arrival rate, concurrency, token distributions).
- We’ll share a short POC recipe and a set of expected p95/p99 matrices for the traffic mix you described.
- Proposed window for a controlled spike test: Tue Dec 8 or Thu Dec 10 (your choice). We’ll need a 4 hour window with a defined traffic script.

On the questions:
- E2E measurement for streaming: by default we report both "first-byte" (time until first token arrives) and "final-token" (time until stream completes) percentiles in our test harness. For SLOs we typically recommend a first-byte p95 target and a final-token p99 target depending on UX needs.
- Concurrency: Hosted supports thousands of concurrent streams per tenant; practical limits depend on model choice and batching settings. We’ll propose an initial ceiling of 600 concurrent streams for the POC (configurable).

I’ll attach the POC recipe and a short expectation table; Aditya — can you add the equipment-level numbers (throughput, per-GPU qps, and guidance on batching pause) into the matrix?

Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_poc_recipe.pdf (PDF, 95KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lopez <s.lopez@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: latency targets & streaming behavior — next steps

Thanks Marcus — digging in on technical specifics below. I mapped Acme's traffic mix to three test profiles (short/medium/long). Key assumptions: network RTT ~ 12–18ms (US region), short prompt avg tokens=28, medium avg tokens=120, long avg tokens=420. Using Redwood-hosted optimized runtime with per-request resizing and KV caching enabled, here are conservative expected numbers for the exact mix you provided (120 reqs/s average, 350 reqs/s burst):

Expected Hosted performance (US-hosted, model: redwood-rlhf-13b-quant, streaming enabled):
- Short interactive (<=40 tokens): first-byte p95 = ~80–110ms, final-token p95 = ~110–160ms, final-token p99 = ~280–360ms.
- Medium (40–256 tokens): p95 final-token ~210–320ms, p99 final-token ~520–820ms (depends on token ceiling).
- Long (>256 tokens): dominated by generation time; throughput oriented - we recommend non-streamed batch endpoints for heavy long requests.

Notes and configuration guidance:
- Measurement: our test harness reports both first-byte and final-token percentiles. For interactive UX we suggest an SLO statement like: "first-byte p95 <= 120ms, final-token p99 <= 450ms" which aligns with your stated targets while accounting for network variance.
- Batching: use continuous batching with a short batching pause (10ms–20ms) to keep per-request latency low while preserving token-level throughput.
- KV caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated context to shave ~15–40ms off final-token latencies for cached prefixes. Cache TTL we recommend 30s for chat sessions.
- Concurrency & autoscaling: we can support 600 concurrent streams safely for your initial POC; autoscaling policy should kick in at 70% utilization. For the Dec test we’ll provision headroom to reproduce your 350 req/s peak without throttling.
- Fallbacks: if an instance becomes overloaded we’ll route to a compatible variant (smaller quantized model) with graceful degradation; we can instrument percent-of-requests-failed-over metric for visibility.

Empirical numbers (internal benchmark, matching your token distributions):
- p95 final-token (combined mix): ~130ms
- p99 final-token (combined mix): ~340ms
- Sustained throughput per provisioned GPU (redwood-rlhf-13b-quant): ~180–220 reqs/s for short interactive requests depending on seq length distribution

Attachments: redwood_latency_matrix.csv (matrix of expected p95/p99 by profile), redwood_test-instructions.md (how we run the spike test).

I’ll also include a short test script (load phases: ramp to 120 reqs/s hold 15m, then 30s bursts to 350 reqs/s x 3) and the exact measurement points (client start, first-byte, final-token). If you want tighter p99 guarantees we can discuss reserved/dedicated capacity as a follow-up.

--
Aditya Rao
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_latency_matrix.csv (CSV, 48KB); redwood_test-instructions.md (MD, 6KB)

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. The performance guidance and spike script look reasonable. We confirmed internal availability for Tue Dec 8 09:00–13:00 PST for the controlled spike test (please confirm).

Two quick follow-ups: 
- Data residency: we need to ensure logs and audit artifacts are stored in US-only buckets. Marcus — can you confirm Redwood Hosted supports US-only logging retention for enterprise customers?
- Cost: please include a rough cost estimate for running the day-long POC (bandwidth + tokens + ephemeral capacity) so our procurement team can pre-approve the spend.

If both items are ok we’ll lock Dec 8.

Best,
Sarah

Acme Analytics
